conflicts.fact: Position of the waterline / what mirror line it corresponds to, and how the line of reflection is expressed
conflicts.versions: Lesson 2 sets the waterline as the x-axis (y = 0). Lesson 3 moves the waterline to y = k, such as y = 2. Lesson 5 hides the waterline and finds it as y = mx + c. Lesson 8 states the waterline is expressible as y = mx + c and the Learned item (2) claims 'the line of reflection can always be expressed in the form y = mx + c', which excludes vertical lines such as x = 3 and x = -1 taught in Lesson 3.

conflicts.fact: Direction of the waterline shift in the explanation vs the setup
conflicts.versions: Lesson 3 overview and predict phase describe the waterline moving up to y = 2 'after seasonal flooding', but the Explained summary says the waterline is 'at any height k above the standard axis' yet the boat reflection lands 'below that new waterline'. The predict phase also places some boat vertices below y = 2, which conflicts with the idea of a reflection of a boat entirely above the water.

conflicts.fact: Mirror orientation and what students observe/predict when moving the boat
conflicts.versions: Lesson 1 uses a flat mirror placed horizontally with thumbs-up/down options (image gets closer vs stays in place), while Lesson 1's Observe says the image appears at an equal distance. Lesson 2's Explained says the water 'applies the rule (x, y) → (x, −y)' with the waterline as the x-axis, whereas the Lesson 2 boat has vertex D(4,0) lying on the x-axis, so the boat touches the waterline and is not 'above' it as Lesson 2's explained states.

conflicts.fact: Whether SSS on a single triangle proves the whole boat is congruent / which condition proves the reflection
conflicts.versions: Lesson 6 says SSS alone is enough to prove the reflected boat image is congruent (Triangle PQR ≅ P'Q'R'), using a triangle. Lesson 7 uses Task 3 (three points) and generalises to the whole boat outline by splitting into many triangles, and states 'SSS is always satisfied'; the Lesson 7 predict phase and Task 2 also use SAS for the symmetric Maasai shield and RHS, so the 'decisive condition' differs by context.

conflicts.fact: Rule for reflection across y = −x and the Maasai task line
conflicts.versions: Lesson 4 Observed says reflecting across y = −x 'both coordinates were swapped and negated' with P(2,−1) → P′(1,−2), which fits (x,y)→(−y,−x). Lesson 8 Task A reflects a Maasai bead pattern across y = x, whereas the Lesson 8 video/observed text describes beads equidistant from a 'central line of symmetry' (a vertical axis in a necklace), so the mirror line used differs.
